quarterly_data.signal: First earnings call as a public company; record quarter. CEO: 'We delivered core revenue of $191.3 million, up 92% year-over-year. Core hardware revenue contributed $111.6 million, up 60% year-over-year, while core cloud and services revenue contributed $79.8 million, up 167% year-over-year.' CFO: cloud pickup came 'as we began our ramp with OpenAI in February, as well as from other customers using the Cerebras Cloud'.
quarterly_data.figure: core revenue $191.3 million, up 92% year-over-year; core hardware $111.6 million (up 60%); core cloud and services $79.8 million (up 167%)

quarterly_data.signal: Margins (CFO): core gross margin 46.5% vs 42.1% a year ago and 41% last quarter; core cloud and services margin 52.9%, driven by 'higher pricing as the market is now valuing higher speed inference at a premium and market demand exceeds supply'; core hardware margin 42% vs 30.6% in Q1 2025 (helped by performance-based incentive pricing; expected to 'return to the low 30s'). To serve contracted backlog sooner Cerebras is 'temporarily renting our own systems back from an existing customer', which will cut core cloud margin by '10-15 margin points' before ramping back toward the 60%+ target. Non-GAAP opex $92.6 million (up 51%, R&D $69.8 million); core non-GAAP operating loss -$3.5 million (-2% margin). Long-term model: approximately 60% gross margin and 40% operating margin.
quarterly_data.figure: core gross margin 46.5%; cloud and services margin 52.9%; hardware margin 42%; rent-back impact 10-15 margin points; core operating loss -$3.5 million

quarterly_data.signal: First guidance (CFO): Q2 core revenue approximately $194 million (88% year-over-year growth), core gross margin 36%-38%, core operating margin -30%--32%. Full year 2026 core revenue $855 million-$865 million (69% growth at the midpoint), core gross margin 38%-41%, core operating margin -28%--32%. Hardware revenue expected to decrease for the next few quarters as production shifts to Cerebras Cloud to fulfil large contracts; second-half growth is 'back end loaded' and comes mainly from 'OpenAI being deployed in our cloud'. Rental costs for the rest of the year 'are baked into Q2 and the annual guide'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 core revenue approximately $194 million (88% growth); FY2026 core revenue $855 million-$865 million (69% at the midpoint); FY gross margin 38%-41%

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted demand: definitive agreement with OpenAI signed December 24, 2025 'for the purchase of more than $20 billion of Cerebras compute over the next several years'; in production by February 1 ('35 days from signature to production deployment'). Binding term sheet with AWS in March, definitive agreement completed the week of the call (AWS impact expected in 2027). CEO: 'we are signing large deals as well, many of which will come on in the first part of 2027' and cited 'we announced 120 MW deal with Bell Canada'. Management declined to size the AWS deal or disclose 10% customers on the call.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $20 billion OpenAI compute commitment; 120 MW Bell Canada deal

quarterly_data.signal: Supply position (CEO): Cerebras sidesteps the industry's binding constraints - 'the binding constraint in the market right now is HBM memory... and we don't use it' (uses on-wafer SRAM); 'The second binding constraint is the CoWoS process at TSMC. We don't use it'; '3 nm capacity at TSMC is a constraint, and again, we don't use it' - Cerebras runs at the 5 nm node. 'We are in the happy position of having supply for our plan and beyond in 2026.' On growth limits: 'Demand is not the constraint. Supply is not the constraint. The constraint is data centers.'

Manufacturing and data centers (CEO): the saleable unit is the CS-3 system (sold on-premise, or as time on Cerebras Cloud / partner clouds); 'we are the only accelerator maker to manufacture exclusively in the U.S.'; 'We have added hundreds of thousands of square feet of manufacturing and clean room space'; expanded partnership with Flextronics and 'added Sanmina as our second major contract manufacturer'. Data centers added across the U.S., Canada, France and the Nordics, with early discussions in Israel, the UAE, Australia, Singapore, India and Indonesia; new data centers coming on 'in Q3, Q4, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 of next year', with discussions with 'literally dozens' of operators ('It's a dog fight out there').

Technology/roadmap: wafer-scale chips '58x larger than the largest competitor' use SRAM instead of HBM; live demo on Kimi K2 (trillion-parameter model) finished in 21 sec vs 4 min and 37 sec on a leading GPU cloud ('13x faster'; CEO's understanding is the GPU endpoint used B300). 'There are only two hardware vendors that currently serve OpenAI models, and we're one of them.' Disaggregated inference (Trainium3 prefill + CS-3 decode with AWS; 'multiple hardware partners') expected 'to begin to deliver in the second half of this year'; CEO sees decode-for-GPU-owners partnerships as real, and Amazon selling Trainium hardware externally as an opportunity.
quarterly_data.figure: 58x larger chip; 13x faster on Kimi K2 demo

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet (CFO): quarter ended with $3.3 billion in cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities; raised $1 billion Series G (September 2025) and $1 billion Series H (February 2026), added a revolving credit facility for up to $850 million (April 2026), then 'completed the largest semiconductor IPO in history, raising another $6.4 billion' - funding to accelerate data-center sourcing and supply chain for the cloud ramp. OpenAI data-center costs are passed through 'with a 3% markup' (reported gross, excluded from core metrics).
quarterly_data.figure: $3.3 billion cash; IPO raised $6.4 billion; revolver up to $850 million
